title: Permission Slip for the Apple Orchard
text:
Dear Families,

On Friday, our class will take a field trip to Happy Hills Apple Orchard. We will leave school at nine o'clock and come back before lunch. At the orchard, students will pick apples, pet a {adjective} goat, and ride on a wagon pulled by a {noun}. The farmer will also teach us how to {verb} like a real apple picker.

Please send your child with a sack lunch, a water bottle, and {number} {plural noun}. Students should wear comfy shoes. Last year someone wore {plural noun}, and they got very muddy. We need three grown-ups to come along. Grown-up helpers must be able to walk {adverb} and count to twenty.

Please sign below and return this slip by Wednesday.

My child may go on the field trip. I promise to pack something {adjective} for lunch.

Grown-up signature: {name}
Favorite kind of apple: {color} and {adjective}

title: What to Pack for the Aquarium
text:
Our class is going to the City Aquarium on Tuesday! Here is your packing list. Please check off each item.

A lunch box with a sandwich, a juice box, and a small bag of {plural noun}. A raincoat, because the dolphins like to {verb} at the front row. A notebook and a pencil for drawing your favorite {noun}. A {adjective} hat so your teacher can find you in the crowd. One stuffed {animal} for the bus ride. Please only bring one. The bus is very full.

Things NOT to pack: fishing poles, buckets, or {plural noun}. The sea turtles get {adjective} when they see those.

Remember, we will be walking {adverb} through the glass tunnel where the fish swim over your head. Please hold hands with your buddy and keep {verb ending in ing}. Our bus leaves at eight o'clock. Please do not be {adjective}!

title: Bus Rules for Field Trip Day
text:
Welcome aboard Bus Number 4! My name is Miss Dot, and I will be your bus driver today. Please listen to these rules.

Rule number one: Stay in your seat. The seats are soft and {adjective}, so this should be easy. Rule number two: Use your inside voice. If you must sing, please sing {adverb}. Songs about {plural noun} are allowed. Rule number three: Keep your hands and your {body part} inside the bus at all times.

Rule number four: Do not {verb} in the aisle. The aisle is only for walking and for my lunch {noun}. Rule number five: If you see a {animal} out the window, you may wave. Last week we saw one, and it {past tense verb} back. Rule number six: No {verb ending in ing} until we get to the museum.

If everyone follows the rules, we will play my favorite game: Spot the {adjective} {noun}. Everyone who plays gets a sticker!

title: Dear Diary, We Went to the Farm
text:
Dear Diary,

Today our class went to Sunny Acres Farm. The bus ride took {number} minutes, and I sat next to my friend Priya. The first thing we saw was a big red barn. Inside, there was a cow named Daisy who was eating {plural noun}. The farmer said Daisy is the most {adjective} cow in the whole state.

Then we got to milk a goat. I was nervous, but I did it {adverb}. The goat looked at me and {past tense verb}. I think that means she liked me. After lunch we went on a hayride. The tractor bumped along the field while we sang songs and tried to {verb}. Priya found a feather that looked just like a {noun}.

At the gift shop, I bought a {adjective} pencil for my little brother. On the way home, everyone fell asleep except our teacher. She was still {verb ending in ing}. Tomorrow I am going to ask Mom if we can get a {animal}.

title: Postcard from the Science Museum
text:
Dear Grandpa,

Greetings from the Science Museum! I am writing this postcard on the bus. The first room had a giant model of a {noun}. It was as tall as a house! A man in a white coat showed us how to make it {verb}. Next we saw the dinosaur room. The sign said this dinosaur liked to eat {plural noun} and nap in the sun. It must have been very {adjective}.

My favorite part was the bubble room. I made a bubble so big that my whole {body part} fit inside. My teacher {past tense verb} when she saw it. In the space room, you can turn a knob and hear what {plural noun} sound like on Mars.

I wish you were here. I got you a {adjective} magnet at the gift shop. It is shaped like a {noun} and says "{silly word}" on it. I will tell you everything very {adverb}.

Love,
Rosie

title: Welcome to the Town History Museum
text:
Hello, students, and welcome to the Town History Museum! My name is Mr. Pickett, and I will be your tour guide today. Please stay with your group. We will walk {adverb} through each room.

In this first room, you can see an old wagon. Long ago, people used wagons to carry flour, wood, and {plural noun} into town. This one was pulled by a {adjective} horse named Clover. Over here is a schoolroom from long ago. Children wrote on little chalkboards and learned how to {verb}. If they were very good, the teacher gave them a {noun} to take home.

This glass case holds the town's first mail bag. Inside, we found a letter that said, "Dear Mabel, please send more {plural noun}." And here is the giant clock. Every hour, a little wooden {animal} pops out and starts {verb ending in ing}.

Today everything in the gift shop costs {number} pennies. Thank you for being such {adjective} visitors!

title: Thank You, Zookeeper Jo
text:
Dear Zookeeper Jo,

Thank you for showing our class around the zoo last week. We had a {adjective} time. Our favorite part was watching the giraffes eat breakfast. We did not know that giraffes like {plural noun} so much. When you fed them, they {past tense verb} with joy. Thank you for letting us touch the turtle's shell. It felt bumpy and {adjective}, like a {noun}.

We also loved the penguins. They walk {adverb} and look like they are wearing tiny {plural noun}. Some of us tried to {verb} like penguins all the way back to the bus.

Our teacher says we can visit again in the spring. When we come back, we will bring you a {food} as a thank-you gift. We hope the lion is still {verb ending in ing} when we get there.

From,
Room 14

P.S. Benji wants to know if the zoo has a {silly word}.

title: Our Day at the Fire Station
text:
Here is our schedule for the field trip to Fire Station 5.

8:30: Get on the bus. Find your buddy and sit {adverb}. 9:00: Arrive at the fire station. Firefighter Lopez will meet us at the door with her dog, Sparky. Sparky is very {adjective} and loves to be patted. 9:15: Tour the fire truck. The truck has ladders, hoses, and a special box full of {plural noun}. We will all get to ring the bell {number} times.

10:00: Firefighter Lopez will teach us how to {verb} like a firefighter. 10:30: Try on a real firefighter helmet. It is heavy and smells a little bit like {food}. 11:00: Snack time in the kitchen. Firefighters cook big meals together. Today they are making {adjective} pancakes with {plural noun} on top.

11:30: Say goodbye. Each student will get a {color} sticker and a picture of a {noun}. 12:00: Ride back to school. Please keep {verb ending in ing} quietly in your seat.

title: Instructions for Field Trip Helpers
text:
Thank you for helping on our trip to the Children's Garden! Here are a few things every grown-up helper should know.

You will be in charge of {number} students. Please count them every time you walk through a gate. They will try to {verb}, but stay calm. Each group has a name. Your group is the {adjective} {plural noun}. Please cheer your group name loudly at lunch.

The garden has many flowers. Please remind students to smell them {adverb} and not to pick them. The roses are very {adjective} this time of year. There is a pond with ducks. The ducks are friendly, but they really like {plural noun}. If a duck follows you, just keep walking and smile.

At noon, we will meet under the big {noun} for lunch. You may sit on a blanket or on a {noun}. If a child asks a question you cannot answer, just say, "Let's ask the {adjective} gardener!"

Thank you for {verb ending in ing} with us today!

title: Kid News Visits the Bakery
text:
This is Channel 2 Kid News with a special report.

Today, Mrs. Hart's second grade class took a field trip to Sugar Moon Bakery on Main Street. The bakery opens very early, so the baker, Mr. Flores, was already {verb ending in ing} when the class arrived. First, the students washed their hands and put on paper hats. Then they learned how to {verb} bread dough. Mr. Flores says the trick is to push it {adverb} and sing to it.

Next, the class made cupcakes. Each student added sprinkles and one {adjective} {noun} on top. Mr. Flores said it was the most {adjective} batch he had ever seen. The best moment came when the big oven beeped. Out came {number} loaves of bread shaped like {plural noun}. The whole class {past tense verb} and clapped.

Every student went home with a cookie and a recipe for {food} muffins. Next year, the class hopes to visit a {noun} factory. Back to you in the studio!
